heightMeaning: WGS84 ellipsoidal height (what Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles use) of the sidewalk at the street line in front of the building = frame z heightRefFrameZ (-1.50). Frame z = 0 (ground-floor FFL +-0.00, the GLB origin) is at frameOriginHeightMetres.

fineTune.note: Corrections found by aligning to the Google tiles (see notes / alignment). Apply as: origin += dx along +x and dy along +y (frame metres), heading += dHeadingDeg, all heights += dHeightM. Keep 0 until measured.
fineTune.measured: Measured 2026-10-31 by the integration pass: node tools/google-check.mjs --mode=measure (Google page load #13: orthographic height map + orthophoto of the Photorealistic 3D Tiles, 192 x 192 m around the site at 0.25 m) then python tools/google-align.py. build-site.mjs copies this block into site.json fineTune.

method.plan: the tiles' building mask (height > street + 3.5 m) matched to the OSM footprints (431 buildings, 75 m radius) by FFT cross-correlation over rotations -3..+3 deg: best shift (-2.09, -3.00) m at 0.0 deg (IoU 0.69 -> 0.81); the best rotation (-0.2 deg) is within the noise (IoU 0.810 vs 0.811), so the OSM heading 214.4 is kept. The plot outline then sits on the old building of no. 161 in the mesh (its roof ~12.9 m above FFL 0) and the street canyon centre agrees.
method.height: carriageway in front of the entrance (x 2..8 m) = 8.35 m lower than the DEM-based prior (55.23 m ellipsoidal) once the 0.15 m kerb is added: the sidewalk at the entrance is ~46.9 m ellipsoidal = ~8.6 m above sea level (EGM2008 N 38.23). Kountouriotou falls ~4.8 % toward +x (south-west): ~ +0.25 m at x 0, -0.35 m at x 12.25 relative to the entrance.

fineTune.status: v3 final (2026-11-01): ONLY the registration of the Google tiles to the building frame remains here (dx, dy, dHeight). It was measured by analysing the tiles' content (see measured) and therefore needs the owner's explicit decision under Google's Map Tiles policy: keep it, or replace it by a registration that does not analyse the tiles. Nothing else in the lab comes from the tiles any more: the tile-ground plane (groundPlane) and the neighbour heights read on the tiles were removed; the receivers' ground and heights are measured on the partner's drone photo (public/ctx/proxies.json).

frame.origin: front-left corner of the plot at the street line (left party wall x street line, as seen standing in the street facing the building), ground-floor FFL level
frame.axes: x along the street line to the right (bearing headingDeg), y into the plot (bearing headingDeg-90), z up; metres
frame.gltf: GLB is Y-up: glTF X = x, Y = z, Z = -y (the street is toward +Z).
frame.gltfRotationNote: gltfRotationYDeg is for a Y-up world with east = +X, north = -Z: model.rotation.y = degToRad(gltfRotationYDeg), model at ENU(lat, lon, frameOriginHeightMetres). 3d-tiles-renderer ReorientationPlugin({lat, lon, height: heightMetres, recenter: true}) instead gives X = WEST, Y = up, Z = NORTH (checked in node_modules/3d-tiles-renderer/src/three/plugins/ReorientationPlugin.js): there, rotate the tiles group by RotY(headingDeg + 90 deg) and lift it by heightRefFrameZ to land in the building frame (or give the GLB rotation.y = -(headingDeg + 90 deg) inside the tiles frame). Self-check: streetCentrelineFrame must lie on the asphalt of the tiles.

geoid.method: median over eudem25m, srtm30m, aster30m, copernicus90 of (street DSM - k x surface lift) = 16.6, 14.4, 21.4, 17.3 m

street.note: streetPolygon = carriageway between our kerb (y -2.3) and a kerb 1.5 m in front of the opposite OSM building line - consistent with the OSM prisms of the fallback. The sources disagree on the width: the OSM building outlines are only 8.83 m apart, the OSM centreline is 6.65 m from ours (off-centre), the app's Street View pano sits at y=-7.42 (agrees with the centreline), the cadastre orthophoto street band is centred near y -6.5, and the renders draw ~12 m between facades. Most likely the real street is 10-12 m wide with its centre at y -6.6..-7.4, i.e. the real facade lines are 1-2 m further out than the OSM roof outlines on one or both sides. Google mode: trust the tiles. Fallback: far-side street trees/lamps belong at y ~ oppositeBuildingLineY + 1.

terrain.note: EU-DEM v1.1 (25 m) - a SURFACE model that reads roofs as well as ground, so only its relative shape is used: zFrame = DEM - DEM(street at the building) + sidewalk z, i.e. the street in front of the building is -1.5 and the rest follows the DEM trend (lower toward the marina to the south, higher toward Kastella hill to the east). Points are local EAST/NORTH metres from the frame origin (not frame x/y), 62.5 m grid; null = water. Indicative only - for a gentle fallback ground; the Google tiles carry the real terrain.

heightRefinement.when: Google mode only, once per page load after the tiles around the site have loaded to full detail (TilesRenderer "tiles-load-end" with nothing pending, camera near the street or overview preset). Exclude our model and the context from the cast (tiles group only).
algorithm: Cast rays straight down (along -up of the local ENU frame) from 300 m above the prior, at the grid samplesFrame.grid (frame metres): 7 positions along the street x 13 across it, so the cast still finds the street when the origin is 1-2 m off across the street.

Turn every hit into an ellipsoidal height: with the ReorientationPlugin frame (origin at lat/lon/heightMetres, +Y up) and the tiles wrapper lifted by heightRefFrameZ, h = heightMetres + (worldHit.y - heightRefFrameZ) (earth curvature is negligible within 50 m); otherwise ECEF -> geodetic h. Ignore misses.

Carriageway level = 20th percentile of the hits with y in [-7.5, -3.0] (the low quantile skips parked cars, trees, awnings). Sidewalk candidate = 20th percentile of the hits with y in [-2.2, -1.6] (outside the balcony line, inside the kerb).

If 0 <= sidewalk - carriageway <= 0.35 m use the sidewalk value, else use carriageway + 0.15 m (kerb). Accept it only if it is within 15 m of the prior (else keep the prior and log both); then heightMetres = that value (frame z -1.50) and frame z = 0 sits 1.50 m higher. Keep the difference as fineTune.dHeightM if it should stick between loads.
Do not sample right at the facades (y > -1.5): balconies and awnings of the old building and the neighbours overhang the sidewalk there. Do not trust one ray: a car roof is 1.5 m, a tree 6 m.

alignment.why: The origin comes from the OSM footprint (+-1.5 m across the street, +-0.5 m along it, +-1.5 m absolute) and the heading from the street axis (34.46 deg over 1280 m of OSM centreline, +-0.5 deg). The Google mesh may be shifted by ~1 m from both.
procedure: Dev overlay (?google=1&align=1): draw plotPolygonFrame, osmFootprintFrame, streetCentrelineFrame and the opposite building line (y = street.oppositeBuildingLineY) as bright lines 0.2 m above the hit ground, with our model hidden and the clip volumes off.

The OSM footprint must sit on the existing building of the mesh, the centreline on the asphalt and the party-wall lines on the roof joints with the neighbours (the left neighbour is lower, the right one higher - visible as steps in the roofline). Nudge: arrows = dx/dy 0.1 m (shift = 1 m), [ ] = heading 0.1 deg, PgUp/PgDn = height 0.1 m; print fineTune JSON to the console to paste into site.json.

Automatic option: ray-cast a 0.5 m height grid over x -20..32, y -14..20 against the tiles, average across x per y row, and fit the two steps (street -> our building line, opposite building line -> street): the step on our side gives dy, the rows at the party walls (x = 0 and 12.23, roof height changes) give dx, and fitting the step line over x gives dHeading.

notes: Heading: the OSM Kountouriotou centreline runs at 34.46 deg over 1280 m, the OSM front edge of no. 161 at 34.33 deg and the dominant building-edge direction within 250 m at 34.2 deg (mod 90) - the Piraeus grid. headingDeg = 214.4 = mean of street and edge, +-0.5 deg. The architect's north arrow gives about 216-217 deg (facade facing 306 deg); it is drawn by hand and disagrees with the map by ~2.4 deg, so it is not used.

Origin: OSM way 203374781 (Kountouriotou 161) is 12.5 x 15.38 m; the plan says 12.23 x 14.5-14.8 m. The plan plot is centred along the street on the OSM footprint (shift -0.07 m from the OSM corner) and its street line is put on the OSM front line, which the neighbours share. The extra 0.6-0.9 m of OSM depth may be old overhangs at the front or over-drawing at the back, so the street line is uncertain by about +-1 m across the street.

Street: OSM centreline 6.65 m in front of our street line; OSM opposite building line 8.83 m. The renders imply ~12 m between building lines; OSM roof outlines on both sides include balconies over the sidewalks, so the real facade-to-facade distance is probably 10-12 m. The street presets keep the camera inside y > -8.

Ground height: Google tiles are WGS84 ellipsoidal. EGM2008 geoid undulation here = 38.2298 m (GeographicLib). Street orthometric height 17 m +-4 m from open DEMs (median over eudem25m, srtm30m, aster30m, copernicus90 of (street DSM - k x surface lift) = 16.6, 14.4, 21.4, 17.3 m). heightMetres = 17 + 38.2298 = 55.23. The Hellenic vertical datum (Piraeus tide gauge) and EGM2008 differ by a few decimetres - irrelevant next to the DEM error. Refine at load (heightRefinement).

Fallback context: OSM footprints extruded from base (frame z; flat at the sidewalk level -1.5; the ground rises toward Kastella hill to the east - see terrain) with OSM heights where tagged, else 4-6 storeys by id. The two neighbours carry heights read from the renders (left G+3 13.85 m, right G+4 15.7 m above the sidewalk).

Presets carry fallbackCheck: probe points on our facade/rear/roof facing the camera and how many are not hidden by the fallback prisms. Occlusion of the rear is real - the Ypsilantou buildings stand ~3 m behind our rear wall.
